title: 💡 A Local Startup Story
text: Aziz started a small delivery company in Termiz two years ago. At first, he worked alone, using his own car to deliver packages around the city. Within six months, demand grew so quickly that he had to hire three drivers. To expand further, Aziz applied for a small business loan from a local bank. The bank approved the loan because his revenue had grown steadily every month. Today, his company employs twelve people and delivers to five cities across Surkhandarya region. Aziz says the biggest lesson he learned was the importance of tracking cash flow carefully — many small businesses fail not because they lack customers, but because they run out of money before payments arrive.

questions.q: Why did Aziz hire more drivers?
Why did the bank approve his loan?
options: He was friends with the bank manager

questions.q: According to Aziz, why do many small businesses fail?
options: They run out of money before payments arrive

title: 🏠 The Shift Toward Remote Work
text: Over the past several years, many companies around the world have allowed employees to work from home, at least part of the time. Supporters argue that remote work increases productivity, since employees avoid long commutes and can better manage their personal schedules. Critics, however, point out that remote work can weaken team collaboration and make it harder for new employees to learn company culture. Some businesses have adopted a hybrid model, requiring staff to come to the office two or three days a week while allowing flexibility on other days. This approach, they claim, offers the best of both worlds — the focus and flexibility of remote work combined with the collaboration benefits of in-person meetings. Whether this trend continues largely depends on how well companies can measure and maintain productivity across different working arrangements.

questions.q: What is one advantage of remote work mentioned in the text?
options: It reduces company costs to zero
It eliminates the need for meetings

questions.q: What is a criticism of remote work mentioned in the text?
options: It is illegal in most countries

questions.q: What does the "hybrid model" refer to?
options: A mix of office and remote work

questions.q: According to the text, what determines whether the remote work trend continues?
options: How well companies can measure and maintain productivity

title: 🤝 A Difficult Negotiation
text: During a negotiation with a foreign supplier, a Uzbek trading company was asked to accept a 15% price increase due to rising raw material costs. Instead of rejecting the offer outright, the company's negotiator proposed a compromise: accepting a smaller 8% increase in exchange for a longer-term contract that guaranteed steady orders for two years. The supplier agreed, since a guaranteed long-term partnership reduced their own business risk. This case illustrates a key negotiation principle — a good deal often comes not from simply refusing demands, but from finding a solution where both sides gain something they value. In this case, the supplier valued stability more than the full price increase, while the buyer valued cost savings more than short-term flexibility.
